notes: Page 2 is a sorting-tips page (sort bricks by colour and lay them out on a table). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.

Page 3 shows the Gandalf minifigure being assembled (hat, head, beard, cape, torso) and a Frodo minifigure. These minifigure parts are not in the supplied parts list, so I added no pieces or joins. The staff is also not recorded here.

Step 1 shows the horse with a 1 x 2 Reddish Brown brick already on its back; I assumed this is lego-3004 from the parts list. Step 2 adds a Reddish Brown 1 x 2 plate on top of that brick. The pieces were placed here as b1 to b3, with the horse as the model's first piece.
The horse's back connection has no port named in the catalogue, so the horse-to-brick join leaves the horse port null.
The pieces (b1, b2, b3) are not given in this return's pieces/rests_on fields because the output schema has no such fields. The same information is encoded as the parts and joined edges.

Page 5 starts a new sub-assembly, apparently the cart base. It is separate from the horse pieces b1 to b3. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.

Step 1: a 1 x 4 plate (b5, Tan) goes on a large plate (b4). I read the large plate as the Dark Tan 2 x 6 (lego-3795); it could be a Tan 2 x 4. Step 2: the Reddish Brown 2 x 4 plate with pins (b6) is placed on b4, then two Dark Tan 1 x 2 plates (b7, b8).

The picture shows only one of the two 1 x 2 plates being placed, and the pin plate already in place. I assumed both 1 x 2 plates rest on b4. The exact stud positions are unclear, so the ports are null. Whether b5 also supports a 1 x 2 plate is unclear.
The pins on b6 are for wheels in later steps.

Step 3 adds a Tan 2 x 4 plate (b9) at the left end of the cart base. Step 4 adds a Reddish Brown 2 x 10 plate (b10) on top. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
The pictures don't show exactly which pieces each plate sits on. I assumed b9 rests on b4 and b6, and that b10 covers b6, b9, b7, b8 and b5. The ports are null because the stud positions are unclear.
The pins on b6 still stick out at the sides of the 2 x 10 plate, for the wheels.

Step 5 adds two Tan 1 x 8 plates (b11, b12) along the long sides of the 2 x 10 plate (b10). Step 6 adds two Light Bluish Gray plates with a clip (b13, b14). The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
I read the grey pieces as lego-92280 (1 x 2 plate with top clip). They could instead be lego-60478 (1 x 2 plate with handle); the picture is small. The parts list has six of each.

The picture shows one clip plate being placed and one already in place near the right end. I assumed one sits on each 1 x 8 plate (b13 on b11, b14 on b12), and the exact stud positions are unclear. The ports are null.

Step 7 adds two Tan 2 x 4 plates (b15, b16) on top of the 1 x 8 plates (b11, b12). Step 8 adds two Dark Tan 1 x 2 plates (b17, b18) and two Light Bluish Gray clip plates (b19, b20) at the left end of the cart. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
The small brownish plates in step 8 are read as Dark Tan lego-3023 (1 x 2 plate), and the grey pieces as lego-92280, as on the previous page.

The pictures are small and the exact stud positions and underlying pieces are guessed, so the ports are null. I assumed b15 and b16 each span both 1 x 8 plates, b17 and b18 sit on b10 and one 1 x 8 plate each, and b19 and b20 mirror the clip plates b13 and b14 at the other end.

Step 9 adds two Dark Tan 1 x 2 plates (b21, b22) and two Light Bluish Gray clip plates (b23, b24), using lego-92280 as before. Step 10 adds two Reddish Brown 2 x 2 jumper plates (b25, b26). The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.

These pieces all sit on the top deck of the tan 2 x 4 plates (b15, b16). Which 2 x 4 plate each piece rests on is a guess. The picture is small, so the ports are null. A piece may straddle both 2 x 4 plates.
The Dark Tan 1 x 2 plates are now all used (6 in the parts list), and so are the six clip plates.

Step 11 builds two side walls (the '2x' box). Each wall is a plate (b27, b28) with two grey handle plates (b29 to b32) fixed to its ends. The walls are then clipped onto the clip plates on the cart deck. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.

I read the wall plates as Dark Tan 2 x 6 (lego-3795), because the 2 x 6 count works out to 3 in the parts list. Tan 2 x 4 plates would give 5 and only 4 are listed. The grey end pieces are read as lego-60478 (handle on end), since six clip plates (lego-92280) were already used on the deck.
The wall-end plates sit on the wall plate's studs, with the grey pieces turned on their sides. I could not see the exact studs, so the wall-plate ports are null.
The handle-plate bars clip into the deck's clip plates. Which deck clips go with which wall is a guess: wall 1 uses b19 and b20, wall 2 uses b23 and b24. The clips are modelled as revolute joins.

Page 11 (step 12) builds a small sub-assembly 4 times: two Tan 1 x 1 bricks and one Tan clip plate (lego-4081b). That uses 8 bricks and 4 clip plates, matching the parts list. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as a repeat with parts and joined edges.
Step 1 shows a brick pushed upside-down onto the clip plate's stud. The picture of step 2 is unclear on how the second brick attaches. I assumed it is held by the plate's clip.
The four corner units are placed on the two side walls (b27, b28). I put one at each wall end, but the exact studs are guesses, and the end studs may be taken by the grey handle plates.
The corner copies are ids corner1 to corner4. The ids b33 and up are not used because the repeat gives its own ids.

Step 13 builds a tailgate: a Dark Tan wedge plate (b33) with two grey handle plates (b34, b35) pushed onto its studs. It is then clipped onto the cart deck's end. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
I read the grey pieces as lego-60478 (handle on end). Two of the six remain after the four used in step 11.

I assumed the tailgate clips onto the two end clip plates b13 and b14, which are the only ones still free, and swings (revolute). The exact wedge studs the grey plates sit on are unclear, so those ports are null.

Step 14 adds the Dark Bluish Gray horse hitching (b36) at the left end, a Dark Tan backpack (b37) and a Reddish Brown barrel (b38) on the deck. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
The hitch is assumed to rest on the left end of the 2 x 10 plate (b10) and the Tan 2 x 4 plate (b9). The ports are null because the picture is small.
The backpack is assumed to sit on the centre stud of jumper plate b25, and the barrel on the centre stud of jumper plate b26. Which jumper takes which piece is a guess.

Step 15 adds one Dark Tan 1 x 2 x 1 panel (b39) at the front of the cart, next to the horse hitch. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
I assumed the panel sits on the Tan 2 x 4 plate (b9) at the left end. It may also touch the hitch b36, but I could not tell from the picture. The exact studs are unclear, so the b9 port is null.
The red arrows show the cart walls folding up. This is a movement, not a new connection, so nothing is added for it.

Step 16 adds four Tan round 1 x 1 plates (cap1 to cap4.rnd), one on top of each of the four corner brick units from step 12. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as a repeat with parts and joined edges.
I assumed each round plate sits on the top stud of the corner unit's first brick (brka). The picture does not show which of the two bricks it goes on, so that choice is a guess.

Step 17 builds a driver's seat: a Tan 2 x 4 plate (b40), a Reddish Brown 1 x 2 plate (b41), a Dark Brown tile (b42) and two Dark Tan panels (b43, b44). It is then placed at the left end of the cart. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
The black piece in the parts box is read as the Dark Brown lego-3069b tile, the only tile of that colour in the parts list. The tile is assumed to sit on the 2 x 4 plate and next to the 1 x 2 plate.
I assumed the seat plate b40 rests on the left end of the cart (b10 and b9). The ports are null because the stud positions are unclear.
This is the fourth Tan 2 x 4 plate (lego-3020), so all four from the parts list are now used.

Step 18 adds a white letter tile (b45) and two Reddish Brown wheels (b46, b47). The finished cart is also joined to the horse. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and joined edges.
The wheels go onto the pins of the pin plate (b6), one on each side, and can spin (revolute).
The horse (b1, b3) is hitched by the horse hitching piece b36. I assumed b36 attaches to the plate on the horse's back (b3).
The letter tile appears at the backpack. I assumed it is held by or against the backpack b37. It could instead be resting on the jumper plate b25, as the picture is small.

Step 19 adds the cargo: a staff made of the grey bar (b53) with a green round brick (b48) and a green cone (b49), a yellow bar (b52) with a white cone (b50), and a red snake (b51). The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and edges.
The bars' round-brick and cone joins are read from the small pictures: the round brick sits on the grey bar, and the cone caps the bar's end. The yellow bar takes the white cone.

The picture does not show how the bars and snake attach to the cart. They stand and lie in the cart bed next to the barrel (b38), so I recorded only loose contact with the barrel. Nothing is clipped to the deck clips, to avoid inventing joins.
The Green round brick and cone are read as lego-3062b and the Green lego-59900 in the parts list.

Step 20 builds a carrot: the Bright Green carrot top (b55) is clipped onto the Orange carrot (b54), then the carrot is placed in the cart bed at the tailgate end. The output schema has no pieces or rests_on fields, so the same information is encoded as parts and edges.
The picture only shows the carrot lying in the cart near the tailgate, not a fixed join. I recorded loose contact with the tailgate wedge b33.
The Gandalf and Frodo minifigures appear in the picture but are not in the supplied parts list, so they are not recorded.
Page 21 is an advertisement for set 9473 (The Mines of Moria). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
Page 22 is a minifigure collection checklist from other Lord of the Rings sets. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
Page 23 is a minifigure collection checklist from other Lord of the Rings sets. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.
Page 24 is the back cover, with a survey advertisement and legal text. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.

Fix 1: b3 (the plate on the horse's back brick, page 4) is retyped from lego-3023 to lego-3794a, the Reddish Brown 1 x 2 jumper plate with one stud. This clears the extra lego-3023 and the missing lego-3794a. The Reddish Brown lego-3023 is b41 (the seat plate). Its joins to b2 are unchanged. The b3 entry here replaces the earlier b3 part.

Fix 2: lego-33009 (book, b56) and lego-63965 (bar 6L, b57) were missing. I could not find a building step for either in the booklet. The 6L bar is Gandalf's staff (page 3) and the book is carried by Frodo (pages 3 and 20). Both are minifigure accessories, and the minifigures are not in the supplied parts list. I record them as parts with no joins, since I would have to invent a minifigure part to attach them to.
Counts checked against the parts list: 3020 x4, 3795 x3, 3023 dark tan x6 plus Reddish Brown x1, 4865b x3, 92280 x6, 60478 x6, 3005 x8, 4081b x4, 6141 x4. These now match.

The cart, horse and cargo form one connected group (the horse is joined to the cart through the hitch b36 and the horse plate b3, and the wheels sit on the pins of b6). The only loose groups were the staff (b57) and the book (b56). They are not built from bricks. They are minifigure accessories, held by Gandalf (page 3 and the page 20 picture, where he sits on the cart seat) and by Frodo (who stands next to the cart).

The booklet gives no step that joins them to the cart, and the minifigures are not in the supplied parts list. To keep one connected model, I added loose contact edges from both to the seat plate b40, as an approximation of the finished model (Gandalf holds the staff on the seat). If these should be treated as separate loose items, these two edges can be dropped.
Everything else is a single connected build. The booklet builds one model, the horse cart.
